learning: If max_error falls below about 0.058 m with line loss at zero, the excursion depends on forward speed, and the speed-versus-progress trade-off becomes the next question. If max_error stays at about 0.061 m, no tested controller or geometry lever moves the excursion, and the remaining question is where in the run it occurs.
notes: Iteration-2 geometry and controller, with base_speed lowered from 1.6 to 1.2 as the single change. Report max_error per track and whether the excursion occurs at the start of the run. Speed is the only lever left untested.
rationale: Iteration 9 tested kd 0.05 to 0.15 on the iteration-2 row and gave identical results (score 26.9949, max_error 0.0614, 0.0611, 0.0609 on oval, s-bend and slalom, zero line loss). Damping therefore does not move the excursion. Across iterations 0 to 9, kp from 2.6 to 4.4, ki 0.3 (confounded with y), footprint, span, mass, wheel_track, wheel_radius and sensor y have all left max_error at 0.061 m. Base speed is the one controller lever not yet tested, and an entry transient or start-up offset would depend on forward speed. I keep the iteration-2 geometry exactly and the iteration-2 controller (kp 3.5, ki 0, kd 0.05, weights [-1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1], last_direction recovery) and change only base_speed, from 1.6 to 1.2, so the race isolates speed. Expected result, which I do not state as measured: line loss stays at zero. max_error moves only if the excursion depends on speed. The trade-off is that lower speed reduces progress per step, so a completion gain is unlikely even if max_error falls.
